short: The Parthenon, a magnificent temple dedicated to Athena, represents the zenith of classical Greek architecture.
full:
Constructed between 447 and 432 BCE during the golden age of Pericles, the Parthenon replaced an earlier temple destroyed during the Persian invasion. Designed by the architects Iktinos and Kallikrates, and overseen by the sculptor Phidias, the building was funded in part by the treasury of the Delian League.

Built entirely of Pentelic marble, the temple is renowned for its refined optical refinements—such as the subtle curving of its columns and base—which correct visual distortions and give the structure a dynamic, organic appearance. It housed a colossal chryselephantine statue of Athena Parthenos and featured elaborate sculptural friezes that celebrated Athenian civic pride and mythology.
